title: ר' חנניא בן חכינאי

paragraphs: (a) Avot, chapter 3. In the Mishnah: Makkot 3:9; Kilayim 4:8, R. Eliezer ben Yaakov in his name. Rambam, in his introduction to Zeraim, writes that he is mentioned only in Kilayim, yet he is also mentioned in Mishnah Makkot, chapter 3, above, 21b.

(b) After marrying and leaving a young daughter, he went to study, with R. Shimon ben Yochai: chapter Af Al Pi. However, there, 62, it says R. Chanina ben Chakhinai was going to the study house at the close of R. Shimon ben Yochai's wedding days. He told him, “Wait for me”—until my wedding days end and I can go with you to study—but he did not wait, etc. Rabbah, Acharei Mot, section 21: R. Chananyah ben Chakhinai and R. Shimon ben Yochai went to study Torah with R. Akiva at Bnei Brak, staying thirteen years. Af Al Pi above says he stayed twelve years at the study house, etc. R. Shimon ben Yochai regularly sent home to learn all their affairs, but R. Chanina did not send to learn what his household had done. His wife sent him, “Your daughter has matured; come and marry her off.” R. Akiva saw through the holy spirit—R. Chanina had not told him—and said, “Whoever has a grown daughter should go and marry her off.” He understood the meaning, took leave, and went. Wishing to enter his house, he found it faced another corner and did not recognize it. He went and sat where women drew water. He heard the girls say, “Daughter of Chakhinai, fill your jar and go up.” He understood she was his daughter and followed her until she entered his house. He entered suddenly after her. His wife barely saw him before her soul departed. He said, “Master of the universe, this poor woman—is this her reward after waiting thirteen years for me?” At that moment her soul returned to her body. End of quotation.

(c) He expounded his words before R. Akiva: Chagigah, chapter 2, 14b. He was R. Akiva's student, as Tosafot writes there; so too the aforementioned Rabbah explicitly says he went to study with R. Akiva, contrary to Rambam, who placed him before R. Akiva's generation. Tosefta Negaim, chapter 1, has R. Chananyah ben Binai speaking in R. Akiva's name; I think it is a scribal error and should read Chakhinai. Ba Siman, Niddah 52b: R. Shimon said, “We found Chananyah ben Chakhinai at Sidon, and he told me: ‘When you reach R. Akiva, etc., tell him: Ben Shelakot testified at Yavneh.’” When he came to R. Akiva, R. Akiva said, “I do not recognize this Ben Shelakot.”

(d) He was one of Yavneh's four sages; see R. Elazar ben Matya. He was one of the five who argued before the sages; see there. Some say he was one of the ten martyrs; others say R. Yehudah the baker, rather than he. He often appears with R. Yosi HaGelili in Sanhedrin, Dinei Mamonot. Menachot 62a: “R. Yosi ben Meshullam says, etc.; R. Chananyah ben Chakhinai says.” Yuchasin, at its end in the gloss on the sequence of tradition from Yesod Olam, writes that R. Yochanan ben Zakkai was his colleague. This is not so: R. Eliezer the Great, R. Yochanan ben Zakkai's student, was the teacher of his teacher R. Akiva. His father R. Chakhinai is mentioned in Pirkei R. Eliezer, chapter 49.
